summary: Milford lookout with a 1911 tree platform and a 1929 steel tower; state-run, cab closed to visitors; height sources disagree (45 ft in 1930, 75 ft in 2021).

facts.design: Steel tower with wood cab; present tower built 1929 per the Register

staffing.status: Staffed by the state during fire season (2016 Register visit note); state towers are manned at fire danger Class 3 or higher (Keene Sentinel)

access.note: Cabin closed to the public per a 2021 hiking guide, which says visitors can climb the tower to the level below the cabin; trailhead is a gated service track off Ponemah Hill Road with room for only a couple of vehicles

visit.drive_up: Gated service track off Ponemah Hill Road, Milford; room for only a couple of vehicles
visit.trail_note: Short, straightforward service track to the tower (per 2021 hiking guide)

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 ft, the height of the 1911 tree platform, not the steel tower. A January 1930 item gives 45 ft for the steel tower, the Register says it was later raised, and a 2021 hiking guide gives 75 ft. Proposed value is the most recent figure found; medium confidence.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Heights disagree: 45 ft in a January 1930 item, raised later per the Register, and 75 ft in a 2021 guide. The record uses the 2021 figure as the latest reported height and the story says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Coordinates differ between NHLR (42.81339, -71.65592) and firelookout.org (42.80479, -71.63033), about 2 km apart; not changed. The 2016 renovation completion is not confirmed by any source read. Access: the cabin is closed per a 2021 hiking blog; the story now says visitors can climb to the level below the cabin, and does not encourage climbing. The NH state fire-tower page returned HTTP 403, so state access and staffing rules are from news and blog sources. Staffing as_of is the 2016 visit date. The 2021 height and access notes rest on one hiking blog.
